gates.label: Integrity and minority protection
gates.reason: Historical Section185 loans and related-party capital decisions deserve scrutiny, but no substantiated diversion, manipulation or severe minority harm is established. Loans were repaid; disclosed corrections and the favorable fraud report are retained.
gates.clearance: Independent valuation/terms for V3 and investments, adjudication outcomes, continuing related party cash transparency.

gates.label: Financial reliability
gates.reason: FY25 inventory EOM is followed by material FY26 March bank stock overstatement 2.61 cr versus books 11.47 cr; repeated prior discrepancies and multiple corrected recognition/control errors make current asset/earnings reliability central. The hold is not for transparent corrections alone and is not an allegation of fraud.
gates.clearance: Bank-acknowledged stock return reconciliation and audited/limited review collection, inventory and sales-cutoff bridge; evidence control remediation has operated, not only been promised.

gates.label: Funding and survival
gates.reason: Completed IPO is meaningful and the conditional base funds old claims and project spending without assumed new debt. Collection/capex stress breaches reserves. A modeled pre-IPO shortfall is a counterfactual, not an observed default; actual historical instalment delays of1–30days are separately disclosed.
gates.clearance: Public IPO-utilization/current cash disclosure and collection/creditor schedule supporting the conditional bridge; distinguish restricted from usable cash.

gates.label: Tradability
gates.reason: BSE SME listing and400-share lot are verified. A dated secondary close is available, but complete20/60-session BSE activity, spread and operative surveillance are not. L is NS; there is no proof of suspension or effective untradability.
gates.clearance: Official BSE activity calendar, turnover/spread and zero-session counts, active SM/ST/trade-to-trade/ASM/GSM notices; rerun lot-aware 5% capacity.

factors.facts: Repeated inventory/bank controls, payment delays and historical Section 185 breaches show stewardship weakness. V3 equipment-for-shares 7.0774 cr and related capital advances require minority scrutiny.
factors.counterevidence: Corrections and related transactions are disclosed; prior offending loans repaid; audit found no material fraud, no willful default. No severe abuse is proven, so no GOV≤3 override.
factors.ceiling: 8 for short operating history/Medium confidence where applicable

factors.facts: Qualified precision processes and rising machining throughput support a useful manufacturing capability; rail and export relationships recur.
factors.counterevidence: No exclusive long-term customer commitment,47.02% single-customer exposure and outsourced bill-to/ship-to integration make surplus contestable. Certificates alone do not establish pricing power.
factors.ceiling: 8 for short operating history/Medium confidence where applicable

factors.facts: Reported three-year growth is extreme and railway/semiconductor expansion demonstrates genuine demand.
factors.counterevidence: Whole-business organic constant-scope growth is not separable from 9 cr acquisitions, new 23 cr engineering services and concentrated integration gross sales. No arbitrary haircut or score 8 from one selected segment.
factors.ceiling: 8 for short operating history/Medium confidence where applicable

factors.facts: Existing rail/semiconductor demand, an operating fourth machining unit and funded new machinery support reachable expansion avenues.
factors.counterevidence: Spring commissioning, cancellable POs and one customer dominate accessible demand. Order values include taxes; broad defence TAM is not secured Millworks business.
factors.ceiling: 8 for short operating history/Medium confidence where applicable

factors.facts: NOPAT/book-capital proxies and physical throughput rise materially; a stable organic capital bridge would be acceptable evidence.
factors.counterevidence: Acquired goodwill/unpaid consideration, V3 noncash equipment, supplier finance, service/integration mix and commissioning lags prevent attributing incremental profits to incremental capital. No product cohort margins to substitute.
factors.ceiling: 8 for short operating history/Medium confidence where applicable

factors.facts: Three-year final-restated CFO-13.029 cr against PAT 44.267 cr; FY26 receivables 138.687 cr and large aged balances persist despite supplier financing.
factors.counterevidence: Most receivables are not due or<6 months, and profit/working capital grew rapidly; nevertheless a multi-year negative realization cannot be excused as capex, which sits in CFI.
factors.ceiling: 8 for short operating history/Medium confidence where applicable

factors.facts: Completed net IPO 152.2384 cr materially improves financeability; March net debt/EBITDA low and no current July default declared.
factors.counterevidence: Only 0.7596 cr March CCE, substantial old tax/seller claims and constrained earmarks; linked collection/capex stress requires equity rescue. No new loans are plugged into gaps.
factors.ceiling: 8 for short operating history/Medium confidence where applicable

factors.facts: Used machine hours 91,450→241,485 over FY24–26 and customers 40→74 show scaling; fourth machining unit operated June–March.
factors.counterevidence: Springs remained commissioning/trial, new acquisitions lack separately measured returns, and order book cash conversion is unproven. Short record precludes exceptional execution scores.
factors.ceiling: 8 for short operating history/Medium confidence where applicable

factors.facts: Core EBIT 49.0719 cr versus 7.4438 cr shows growth is not merely interest income; normalized earnings per current share remain positive after IPO dilution.
factors.counterevidence: FY26 services 23 cr and investment/customer mix change recurrence; FX 4.41 cr and deferred tax credit 2.6292 cr flatter reported PAT. Historical 30.67 EPS must not be used with current 17,614,755 shares.
factors.ceiling: 8 for short operating history/Medium confidence where applicable

factors.facts: Dated price 1069 and full funded base sensitivity are calculated; base return is approximately flat at 15 × exit EBITDA.
factors.counterevidence: Current decision-eligible return not established while financial reliability is on hold; conditional forecasts do not qualify as ordinary supported returns. No neutral score substitutes.
factors.ceiling: 8 for short operating history/Medium confidence where applicable

factors.facts: Combined customer/collection/margin shock breaches cash reserves and causes hypothetical dilution; book assets largely receivables and acquisition goodwill.
factors.counterevidence: Completed IPO, ongoing rail growth and unmodified going-concern language mitigate near-term failure. Low leverage alone is not downside protection at 1069.
factors.ceiling: 8 for short operating history/Medium confidence where applicable

factors.facts: Current-share reported P/E is roughly 51 x and normalized multiple roughly 60 x; funded reverse model requires strong sustained growth despite multiple normalization.
factors.counterevidence: Genuine expansion and IPO-funded capacity could deliver stronger earnings; bull is not impossible, but uses materially better collections/margins than base.
factors.ceiling: 8 for short operating history/Medium confidence where applicable

factors.facts: Lot 400 costs 427600 at reference 1069; a 500000 reference can buy one lot but not two.
factors.counterevidence: Actual 20/60 day BSE turnover, spread, zero sessions and active restriction not verified. Liquidation capacity cannot be inferred from NSE absence or dynamic volume widgets.

cash_claims_policy.investments: Quick Pay at cost5.7506 and Vidwan conversion2.748522235 receive zero terminal uplift. Vidwan incremental1.472422235 exposure is assumed cash use conservatively between21July and31August, because31August filing says the full loan is already outstanding, not another2.7485 conversion outflow. cash_claims_policy.old_obligations: Old income tax, MSME interest, statutory dues, CSR, all0.4645 accrued employee-benefit provisions and seller consideration settled separately, excluded from opening operating WC. No principal double count.
cash_claims_policy.project_commitments: 22.9602 net capital commitments assumed included within61.0325 IPO project; sensitivity treats wholly additional. Existing4.9232 capital advances are already spent; not charged again.

These are analyst reserve assumptions, not legal covenants or evidence of default.
cash_claims_policy.eligibility: Earmarked capital and WC pools meet only corresponding eligible uses; unspent pools excluded from equity value, not freely used for old taxes/seller/debt. No borrowed money plugged into deficits.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. Millworks has built a real precision-manufacturing operation, but current asset reliability and cash realization do not support an evidence-backed compounder designation. Its extraordinary revenue jump is not a software growth story. Concentrated customer/investment exposure, new engineering services, outsourced integration and acquisitions change the economics being measured. The completed IPO is a substantial funding positive, not unrestricted surplus cash. At the dated ₹1,069 reference, the base model produces roughly flat five-year return under multiple normalization. No ordinary return, actionable entry price or numerical rank is eligible while G2 remains on hold. [E02–E06, E12, E17, E24]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Millworks Technologies Limited, CIN U29200KA2021PLC153863, was incorporated on 1 November 2021. The security is BSE SME 544826 / MILLWORKS / INE1SRC01010, with 17,614,755 issued shares, ₹10 face value and a 400-share lot. Information cutoff is 20 October 2026; market reference is 19 October, before the Dussehra holiday. Valuation runs from 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, using 1,826 actual days divided by 365.25. Latest audited year: 31 March 2026. No accessible comparable H1 FY2027 results were available by cutoff. Historical accounts and forecasts are standalone. Proposed Vidwan ownership is not presumed consolidated without completion evidence. Financial retrieval confidence is High; organic growth and capital attribution Low; current cash and valuation Medium and conditional; implementation Low. Overall confidence for a favorable investment conclusion is Low because material evidence is incomplete, not because the documentary warnings are unverified. [E01, E03, E10, E20, E21] Accounting basis: Indian GAAP under Accounting Standards (AS), not Ind AS, per S03 F9.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: All 13 factors below have material facts, counterevidence, confidence and evidence IDs. Integer scores or NS use exact Decimal weights and HALF_UP rounding to one decimal. BQS and GQS are incomplete because REV and CAP are NS. IAS also lacks usable Q, R and L, and G2 excludes favorable investment conclusions. Missing scores receive neither zero nor 5. Mathematical bounds are not confidence intervals or rankable estimates. Persistent CASH 2 activates a GQS ceiling of 5, but the aggregate remains NS. GOV 4 does not activate the severe-governance cap. Moving GOV or MOAT by one point changes the BQS known contribution by 0.20 each; moving DUR changes BQS by 0.10 and GQS by 0.20. None resolves the missing factors.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The business makes customer-specified machined parts, fabricated sheet metal and subassemblies, generally in high-mix production. Rail applications include braking, door, coupler and pantograph components; aerospace, defence and semiconductor equipment require precision and approvals. This is an industrial supply-chain business, not recurring software. Parts sales and engineering/design services have different recognition and collection economics. The disclosed service policy uses time-and-material execution. In the dominant defence relationship, supplier Big Bang Boom Solutions provides facilities and integration; Millworks personnel work there, and some goods ship directly from supplier to customer under bill-to/ship-to arrangements. Gross reported sales cannot therefore be valued as if every rupee were proprietary in-house machining value added. [E02, E05, E06]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Qualification, tolerances and accepted manufacturing processes can create switching costs because buyers must requalify parts and suppliers. Rising machine usage and recurring rail/export relationships support a useful position, but no full-cycle pricing-power record is established. Cancellable purchase orders, buyer concentration, outsourced integration and competing qualified shops limit bargaining power. No verified market-share denominator, switching-time measure or contractual price escalator is disclosed. Top-ten customers supply 92.06% of sales, and the largest 47.02%; customer logos are not a moat. Supplier and customer concentration must be assessed together. [E02, E05, E07, E08]

Peers provide economic context, not a borrowed valuation premium. Unimech supplies high-mix aerospace tooling/components; Azad emphasizes qualified engine components and long-duration OEM contracts; MTAR spans clean energy, space and defence engineering. End markets, margin definitions, subsidiary perimeters and contract duration differ. Prospectus peer prices are from June 2026, not October. No unverified current peer multiple justifies the model's terminal assumptions.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Reported revenue rose from ₹1.774 crore in FY2023 to ₹148.767 crore in FY2026, with final-restated FY2024/FY2025 at ₹9.386/22.1001 crore. The three-year reported CAGR below is not an organic CAGR. Five- and ten-year CAGRs are unavailable, not zero: incorporation was in 2021 and FY2022 was a zero-sales startup stub. The low starting base is not separately penalized after comparability is addressed. FY2026 sector sales excluding drawback were defence ₹103.2582 crore, rail ₹35.1719 crore, semiconductor ₹8.835 crore and aerospace ₹1.4681 crore. Rail more than doubled and semiconductor nearly doubled, so dismissing all growth as acquired or accounting growth would be wrong. Nevertheless, ₹23 crore of new services, ₹69.9276 crore from Quick Pay and undisclosed acquired-business contribution prevent a whole-business organic growth basis. No arbitrary acquisition haircut is invented and no selected rail series substitutes for comparable whole-company CAGR. [E03, E06, E07, E09]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Used machine hours increased from 91,450 to 157,660 to 241,485 in FY2024–2026. FY2026 productive capacity of 322,938 hours implies 74.78% utilization. Including 60,081 spring commissioning hours produces 63.05%, but that is not a mature productive-capacity denominator. Four units and IPO machinery support expansion while spring production remains in trial. Revenue per machine hour and profit per employee are not comparable unit economics because integration, electronic materials and services changed the mix. The disclosed-cost value-added proxy rises in rupees but falls as a sales percentage. No reliable volume/price/constant-currency/acquired-margin bridge is provided. CAP remains NS despite high accounting proxies: acquisition goodwill and unpaid seller consideration, noncash related-party equipment, vendor finance and commissioning lags prevent attribution. A coherent organic capital bridge or suitable cohort economics could clear CAP; private project data specifically are not required. A nominal INR industrial cost-of-capital range of 12–18% is a sensitivity, not proof that current ROCE measures excess incremental returns. [E08, E09, E11, E16]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Founder-led operating execution is visible in throughput and customer additions, but stewardship requires more than growth. Promoter-plus-group ownership declines from 65.08% to 47.18% through the fresh IPO; this is dilution, not promoter selling in the issue. Promoters alone hold 42.93%, with the promoter group 4.25%. V3 supplied ₹7.0774 crore of machinery for equity in FY2025. Related rent and capital advances are material and need commercial-term scrutiny. Historical Section 185 loans from FY2024–2025 were repaid by March 2026; they are not currently outstanding violations. Adjudication and filing outcomes still merit follow-up. A disclosed related-party transaction is not automatically abusive. Latest CARO identifies short instalment delays and irregular statutory remittance, but no willful default, material fraud or one-year material uncertainty. The July prospectus reports no current default or rescheduling. FY2025's inventory emphasis and recurring backup exceptions qualify the clean-main-opinion headline. [E14–E16]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Use final-restated FY2024–2026 consistently for cash conversion. Capital spending explains weak free cash flow, not negative operating cash flow: receivables are the principal operating drag, partly financed by suppliers. FY2026 closing receivables of ₹138.6868 crore are 93.22% of sales. Average receivable days of 178.48 differ from closing days of 340.27 because sales expanded rapidly. Not-due balances of ₹62.6651 crore and balances under six months of ₹47.7277 crore argue against calling all receivables overdue. However, ₹27.701 crore at six to twelve months and ₹0.5930 crore older remain material. Base assumes no blanket bad-debt deduction; bear tests loss of 20% of opening receivable collections. Cash capex includes advances and cannot be treated entirely as maintenance. Electronic-material purchases of ₹40.9627 crore corroborate the integration mix change.

Transparent restatement is not itself misconduct. Corrections include sales timing, inventory, power costs, rent/salary capitalization, useful lives, MSME interest and tax. Original FY2025 statutory, later statutory comparative and final-restated cash flows must remain separate. FY2026 statutory CFO of minus ₹1.6247 crore becomes restated minus ₹10.7629 crore, with offsetting CFI/CFF regroupings and essentially identical closing cash. Acquisition consideration payable contaminates the statutory operating-liability movement; it is not sustainable customer cash. Current bank stock of ₹14.08 crore versus ₹11.47 crore in books, after the earlier inventory emphasis, remains a material reliability issue. The issuer's clerical/year-end explanation and favorable physical-inventory/IFC findings are retained as counterevidence. [E04, E11–E15, E19]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The ₹1,069 reference comes from the dated 19 October historical row, not the 21 October live quote. Market capitalization uses 17,614,755 current shares rather than FY2026's 12,084,550 weighted-average EPS denominator. Current-share reported EPS is approximately ₹21.04, not ₹30.67. The normalized alternative excludes ₹4.6297 crore of other income and uses a 31.2% cash-tax assumption. Realized FX can be economically operating, so excluding all FX is conservative rather than a claim that it is fictitious.

Exit value uses FY2032 full-year run-rate EBITDA and 8/15/20 times for bear/base/bull. Base's 28% margin is below FY2026's reported 35%, with ₹0.5 crore of recurring overhead escalating 5%. Maintenance capex of 3% of sales plus growth capex of 14% of incremental revenue continues after IPO. The ₹61.0325 crore project is funded only from its designated pool. Existing net commitments are assumed within that budget; an additional-commitment stress removes the overlap. Operating rent remains in EBITDA; no duplicate lease debt or property uplift is added.

Earmarked IPO capital and working-capital pools cannot fund old tax, seller claims or principal. General proceeds and generated cash fund those uses. Fee relief of ₹0.6 crore is an explicit estimate of previously paid costs, tested from zero to ₹0.7434 crore with the opening working-capital balance adjusted consistently. Quick Pay conversion is not charged again. The incremental Vidwan exposure is conservatively paid by 31 August, when the announced loan was already outstanding; conversion itself is noncash. Subsidiary profit and NCI are both excluded. Unspent earmarks receive no terminal equity value. Conditional entry values are not actionable buy prices while G2 is on hold. [E17–E25] Base assumes the ₹5.9584 crore bank overdraft and ₹0.6903 crore director demand loan remain outstanding through exit. A full ₹6.6487 crore call/no-renewal stress repays them from unrestricted cash on 31 October 2026, without using earmarked IPO pools. The terminal earnings year is 1 April 2031–31 March 2032, capitalized on 20 October 2031; it is not exact next-twelve-month earnings. Daily uses precede same-day receipts under an explicit uniform-flow assumption. The pre-IPO reserve is ₹0.25 crore, approximately one week of FY2026 payroll and rent, with ₹0.5/1 crore sensitivities. Post-IPO reserve is ₹3 crore, tested at ₹5 crore; terminal reserve is the greater of ₹3 crore or 2% of run-rate sales. FY2027 sales before IPO use at most a ₹180 crore annualized rate; additional bull sales begin only after capital receipt. Flat pre-IPO working capital is a material collection assumption, stressed with ₹10/20 crore extra absorption. All post-March balances are estimates, not verified October bank balances. The daily receipt/use test is a net-working-capital timing proxy: it does not separately reconstruct gross customer collections and supplier repayments. Consequently its daily trough is conditional and does not guarantee actual intraday liquidity. Separate collection and supplier calendars would be needed to verify that timing.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The central thesis breaker is failed collection of concentrated customer receivables without further financing, not a share-price decline. Lower orders and margins combine with new fixed costs, slower inventory, old tax and seller claims, and restricted project money. Bear uses ₹125 crore FY2027 sales, 19% EBITDA margin, 300 receivable days, 70 inventory days, 90 payable days, a 15% project overrun and loss of 20% of March receivable collections. Cash floors are breached before entry and later. Ordinary and conditional non-rescue returns and entry values are therefore NULL. An unfunded terminal accounting value is not a realizable target. The rescue diagnostic explicitly prefunds uses with whole shares, 5% issue fees and a 35% issue-price discount, then measures dilution. This is hypothetical funding, not a committed facility or an assertion of actual historical default. Permanent-loss risk is High because receivables, goodwill and customer investments provide uncertain downside protection. Counterevidence is meaningful: completed IPO, genuine rail growth, no current July default and favorable IFC/going-concern language. [E05, E09, E11, E14, E17, E24]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five-year 5× and 10× stock outcomes require approximately 37.98% and 58.50% annualized price growth, not merely similar revenue growth. Target capitalization uses current shares before new dilution. The solver varies uniform FY2028–2032 revenue growth while retaining base margin, working-capital requirements, reinvestment, reserves and a 15-times terminal multiple. Only finite funded adjacent brackets qualify, and root residuals are checked. A cash-constrained endpoint is never reported as a solution. Neither 5× nor 10× has a funded root over the tested minus 10% to 100% growth range. Both are Speculative / unsupported under these economics, not mathematically impossible under all future business models. A credible case needs better value added or collection terms, proven capital returns and explicit financing/dilution rather than an assumed rerating. [E24, E25]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: The nine checks below distinguish warning signs from thesis breaks. Priority is evidence of collections and operating control remediation, not another order headline. A first post-IPO limited review and utilization statement could update funding and growth without demanding private daily bank records. Implementation requires verified BSE trading conditions and lot-aware turnover; a 400-share lot does not guarantee an exit. No automatic monitor or trade has been created.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Classification: Hold — unresolved, with insufficient evidence for complete quality and growth scores. This is not an evidence-backed compounder candidate. Research priority is collection/control validation and acquired-business/service unit economics. The company is not eligible for favorable investment consideration or a numerical rank at the cutoff. This is not Avoid — governance because severe abuse is not substantiated, and not a current funding-failure classification because counterfactual model stress is not observed insolvency. A cheaper share price alone cannot resolve G2. An existing-holder decision would need the user's position, liquidity and tax context; none is invented.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary filings support the historical financial and audit analysis; source URLs, document vintages and material limitations are listed below. Some later exchange attachments were unavailable, so mirrored issuer text or secondary summaries are explicitly distinguished from primary files. The dated market reference is secondary, and complete BSE liquidity data remain unverified. Open questions are bank-accepted stock reconciliations, customer collections and Quick Pay economics, service/acquired-business profit and capital breakouts, actual IPO utilization and prepaid fees, Vidwan completion, and current BSE restrictions/activity. The 19–20 October capability and personnel announcements provide context only, with no modeled financial uplift. News dated 21 October is outside the cutoff. Forecasts are assumptions, not historical facts. [E10, E12, E17, E21, E23–E25]

summary: Hold — unresolved. Millworks has built a real precision-manufacturing operation, but current asset reliability and cash realization do not support an evidence-backed compounder designation. Its extraordinary revenue jump is not a software growth story. Concentrated customer/investment exposure, new engineering services, outsourced integration and acquisitions change the economics being measured. The completed IPO is a substantial funding positive, not unrestricted surplus cash. At the dated ₹1,069 reference, the base model produces roughly flat five-year return under multiple normalization. No ordinary return, actionable entry price or numerical rank is eligible while G2 remains on hold. [E02–E06, E12, E17, E24]
